narrative.scqa_md:
Kitsap Credit Union is a $2.5B in assets credit union regulated by NCUA, operating since 1934 with 325 employees. A 11.2% multi-year growth rate and a trajectory the analyst classifies as stable give it the balance sheet to fund transformation [E-078, E-016]. Zennify's assessment places overall digital maturity at 2.6/5. The deepest capability gap is Champions Program at 2.1/5 against a 2.6 peer median [E-083]. Next is Reconciliation Automation at 2.2/5 against a 3.0 peer median [E-069, E-076].

Third is Third-Party Risk Framework at 2.2/5 against a 2.7 peer median [E-054]. The issue register adds capability weights sum to 100 per CATEGORY (authoritative Pillar toolkit; direct capability->category aggregation)… (critical severity). The issue register adds Per-row single Tier column vs multiple cited E-IDs of differing tiers across all columns -> 752 'mismatches' (critical severity). Counter-signal: Technology Strategy already runs at 3.4/5 against a 2.6 peer median — a strength to build on, not rebuild. The roster shows no CISO — a named ownership gap for the capabilities below.

The question for Kitsap Credit Union is whether to close Champions Program first — the constraint the other investments inherit — or continue layering point solutions on top of it and accept the compounding operating cost. Kitsap Credit Union should lead with Tableau (68/100 fit) against Risk Appetite & Framework, then sequence nCino behind it. Closing Champions Program to the peer median alone is worth 0.5 maturity points, and the capabilities that depend on it compound the gain. The analyst's own priority framing: "Soft employee wellbeing = adoption risk — Indeed 3.4/5, wellbeing 'Low', CEO approval 69.7%, recommend ~49% [E-083] — Change-adoption risk for enterprise rollouts…".
